Exercise 15.7.30 — Six Iterated Integrals over a Circular Cylinder

Problem. Express the integral ∭Ef(x,y,z) dV \iiint_E f(x,y,z)\, dV ∭E​f(x,y,z)dV as an iterated integral in six different ways, where EEE is the solid bounded by the surfaces y2+z2=9,x=−2,x=2. y^2 + z^2 = 9, \qquad x = -2, \qquad x = 2. y2+z2=9,x=−2,x=2.

Part 1 — The six orders of integration

Step 1.1: Describe the solid.

The surface y2+z2=9y^2 + z^2 = 9y2+z2=9 is a circular cylinder of radius 333 about the xxx-axis. The two planes x=−2x = -2x=−2 and x=2x = 2x=2 cap it, so the solid is the cylinder segment E={(x,y,z):−2≤x≤2,  y2+z2≤9}, E = \{(x,y,z): -2 \le x \le 2,\; y^2 + z^2 \le 9\}, E={(x,y,z):−2≤x≤2,y2+z2≤9}, of length 444 in the xxx-direction. Every cross section perpendicular to the xxx-axis is the full disk y2+z2≤9y^2 + z^2 \le 9y2+z2≤9, and every cross section perpendicular to the yyy- or zzz-axis is a rectangle of half-width 9−(other)2\sqrt{9 - (\text{other})^2}9−(other)2​.

Step 1.2: The six iterated integrals.

The variable integrated first spans a symmetric interval; the remaining two variables fill the disk y2+z2≤9y^2 + z^2 \le 9y2+z2≤9 in either order:

Derivation of the limits. In any order, the variable that is not yyy or zzz runs freely over its full interval (xxx over [−2,2][-2,2][−2,2], or yyy or zzz over [−3,3][-3,3][−3,3]). The two variables remaining in the disk y2+z2≤9y^2 + z^2 \le 9y2+z2≤9 are split by solving the disk inequality for the inner one: if zzz is innermost then −9−y2≤z≤9−y2-\sqrt{9-y^2} \le z \le \sqrt{9-y^2}−9−y2​≤z≤9−y2​ with −3≤y≤3-3 \le y \le 3−3≤y≤3; if yyy is innermost then −9−z2≤y≤9−z2-\sqrt{9-z^2} \le y \le \sqrt{9-z^2}−9−z2​≤y≤9−z2​ with −3≤z≤3-3 \le z \le 3−3≤z≤3. Arranging the three variables in all six possible orders gives the integrals above.

Step 1.3: Verification by Python.

The script solution/part1_step1.py evaluates all six orders with the constant integrand f=1f = 1f=1 using SymPy. Every order returns the exact volume 36π≈113.097336\pi \approx 113.097336π≈113.0973, confirming that the six sets of limits all describe the same cylinder segment. The figure script part1_figure1.py produces the figure embedded above.
